significance.justification: Verified true, the claim would license the form-(iii) law that "transfer ... is a monotone function of typological distance," with semantic components tracking lexical/genetic distance and syntactic circuits tracking word-order/morphological distance; this fixes expected transfer orderings across languages and distinct regression profiles across component types rather than merely asserting shared representations. It establishes a cross-lingual phenomenon at the level of causally effective components and a limited mechanistic decomposition of reuse, although it does not explain why those typological dimensions control the components; this would sharpen language-selection explanations currently based on task-level transfer patterns, as in Pires et al.'s 2019 mBERT study and Lauscher et al.'s 2020 zero-shot transfer analysis. The true and false states are distinguishable, and a negative result would materially rule out typological distance as a monotone component-level predictor or the proposed semantic/syntactic dissociation, though it would not identify the replacement account. In the topic-substitution check, the generic question of language-independent versus language-specific mechanisms would not earn this score; the specific distance-conditioned, feature-type-dependent law is what places the claim above the topic median.

reach.justification: The named handles are the "per-component transfer score" and the "variance in transfer explained by each distance dimension," combined into the claimed ability to identify "which languages will fail to inherit which capabilities." The fitted score is post hoc, but the typology-to-transfer relation is an ex-ante predictor because known language distances could forecast weak reuse before attempting deployment or adaptation, giving model auditors and multilingual-training practitioners an action window. After recalibration on another model, the substantive conclusion predicts a monotone ordering and component-specific distance profile rather than merely supplying a procedure for searching, although the hypothesis does not explicitly guarantee invariance across architectures or training recipes. The topic alone supplies no comparable handle in the substitution check; reach comes from this transferable predictor across languages and component classes, not from multilingual modeling's general importance.
